sam: Quick question after doing a 10-min run on the compact notify row: when rows are dense and some channels are suppressed, what announce order makes the most sense for screen readers? I attached a tiny clip: https://redwood-internal.screenshots/compact-sr-clip.mp4 anya: Thanks. my vote is: severity first, then channel, then suppression state, then recent count. e.g. "Critical, Database Alerts, notifications suppressed, 2 recent messages" so people hear triage signal immediately. leah: I hear that, but a few customers prefer context-first (channel then severity) for mental-model reasons. we should default to severity-first but document as a toggle for enterprise prefs. mike: Implementation FYI: if we put everything in aria-label, keep visual badges aria-hidden to avoid duplicate speech. also prefer verb phrase for state ("notifications suppressed") not a single badge word. preeti: tiny copy nits: change menu item from "Snooze" -> "Snooze notifications" and tooltip to "Snooze notifications for this channel". also announce counts as "2 recent messages" not "2 previews". ux-bot: Accessibility snippet suggestion: ```html
Critical Database Alerts
``` leah: Note: aria-live should be on the preview container only. avoid aria-live on the whole row or focus events will trigger redundant speech in some readers. mike: Keyboard order debate: keep preview toggle before overflow menu to maintain LTR flow; ensure both are focusable with no delay on action handlers. anya: I'll add these as acceptance criteria: severity-first default (with enterprise opt-in for channel-first), suppression state as verb phrase in aria-label, preview announced via aria-live only on expand, snooze copy updates, preview toggle focusable. I’ll mock a small prototype for SR testing tomorrow and tag @preeti for copy review. sam: perfect — thanks. can we also add a prefers-reduced-motion note for the expand animation? some SR users prefer static reveals. anya: Good catch. adding it now to the ticket INF-1501 and the Figma notes. preeti: I'll review copy and submit PR for menu labels after the prototype looks good. sam: great, pairing session Friday morning for VoiceOver + NVDA testing? leah: I'm in. :thumbsup:
